CENTRA

A dashboard concept that gathers the daily work of public transport planning staff in one place. Developed with Team 02 for MVG/SWM in Munich.

DashboardUser ResearchPrototypeLogo
My roleResearch, concept, prototype, logo
ContextUX3 block course, Team 02
UsersMVG/SWM staff
ToolFigma
The context

Intelligent Urban Systems

UX3 is a block course on Concept Development at LMU Munich. The 2026 theme was Intelligent Urban Systems: digital systems woven into everyday city life, from ticket machines to adaptive traffic lights.

Our team of eight took public transport as its field and chose the people behind the timetables as its users: MVG/SWM planning staff.

The research
8

Interviews with MVG employees

Over the first three project days we spoke to staff from different departments, most of them driver and shift planners (Fahr- und Dienstplaner:innen). Each session began with introductions and a walk through the systems they use, then moved on to a typical workday.

What we heard

Three recurring pain points

1Storage problems
2A confusing program structure
3Unnecessary, repetitive work steps
HASTUSDIVAProFahr
The idea

One starting point for the daily tools

Staff work across several specialised programs. Instead of opening each one to find out what is waiting, CENTRA is the screen they land on: tasks, tickets, colleagues and data transfer in one view, with direct links into Diva, ProFahr, Hastus and the team blog.

The concept

Four modules on the dashboard

Deine To-Do’s

A personal task list for the day, always the first thing you see.

Tickets

Omnitracker and Autoticket side by side, with colour-coded rows to tell items apart quickly.

Team Ansicht

What each colleague is working on, where they need help and until when they are available, with shortcuts to chat, mail, call or ticket.

Daten Export

Pick a source and a target program, preview the timetable data and follow the optimization progress.

A side panel collects notifications and messages such as timetable changes and maintenance windows, so nothing gets lost between systems.

My contribution

From interviews to prototype

I took part in all project phases, from the interviews through concept to prototype. I built the prototype in Figma and designed the CENTRA logo: four connected stops on a line, like a route map.

3 Days Later

A five-person production. A thriller about a disappearance, a prime suspect, and a case built entirely on circumstantial evidence. Shot, scored and cut by our team over one semester.

Short FilmWritingEditingSound
RoleCo‑writer, editor, cast, sound
ToolsDaVinci Resolve, Audacity
DeliverablesFilm, posters, teaser, site
TimeframeApril – July 2026
My part

Across the full pipeline

I co‑wrote the script, appeared on screen as the lead suspect, cut the intro and several post‑production sequences, built AI‑generated video inserts and shaped the sound design. Alongside the film, I designed the character and film posters and a promotional website.

The poster follows an intentional visual language: minimal, dark, and quietly unsettling. A single object does the emotional work instead of a crowded frame.

Web Development · Medientechnik Praktikum

3 Days Later — Promo Site

A case‑file website for a short film. Built like a police dossier: a stamped “VERTRAULICH” teaser, one file per person involved in the case, then the official film and character posters.

HTMLCSSJavaScriptResponsive
RoleDesign & front‑end
StackHTML, CSS, vanilla JS
InteractionHover, tap & keyboard
LanguageGerman
How it works

Cast cards that open like folders

Hover, tab to a card or tap it and the file slides open with the character’s status and backstory. One file is open at a time, a click elsewhere closes it, and Enter or Space work from the keyboard.

It is plain HTML, CSS custom properties and about 30 lines of vanilla JavaScript, with no framework. The layout reflows for phones and respects reduced‑motion settings.

UI/UX Concept · Figma

SynchroTrack

A dynamic sonic focus companion. A concept app where sound adapts to how you want to feel.

Mobile UIUX FlowConcept
RoleUI/UX design
ToolFigma
Screens6 core screens
FocusState‑driven visual system
The idea

Pick a state, get a session

Pick a target state: Calm Focus, Medium Drive or High Energy, and the app plays a session tuned to it, with a running timer to track how long you stay in flow.

My part

The full first‑time flow

An onboarding splash, authentication, a mood‑selection screen built around three tactile spheres, and three session screens whose gradients shift from cool and quiet to warm and driven. The color itself communicates intensity before you’ve read a word.
